WPL 2027 Mini-Auction Highlights

Australian all-rounder Sophie Molineux secured the highest bid of the Women's Premier League (WPL) 2027 mini-auction, commanding a price of 1.10 crore rupees from UP Warriorz. Molineux, who entered the auction with a base price of 50 lakh rupees, drew intense interest before UP Warriorz successfully outbid Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to secure her services.

Top Acquisitions and Team Investments

Among Indian players, aggressive batter Kiran Navgire emerged as the costliest domestic buy, joining Delhi Capitals for 75 lakh rupees to bolster their middle order. Meanwhile, Gujarat Giants invested in young talent Gunalan Kamalini for 40 lakh rupees. Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru secured veteran Australian spinner and all-rounder Jess Jonassen at her base price of 40 lakh rupees.

Additionally, seven players attracted uniform bids of 30 lakh rupees each. UP Warriorz added Grace Harris, Sneh Rana, Sushma Verma, and Asha Sobhana to their roster at this price point. Gujarat Giants signed Orla Prendergast, while Royal Challengers Bengaluru acquired Tejal Hasabnis and Chloe Tryon for 30 lakh rupees each.
